title: Bread (Reduced Calorie/High Fiber, White or NFS)

content.title: About
content.content: Bread is a baked product made from dough, typically consisting of wheat flour, water, yeast, and salt. Reduced‑calorie and/or high‑fiber versions are produced with added whole‑grain flour, bran, seeds or specialized fibers, making them more nutritious and lower in calories than traditional white bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bread is one of the oldest foods, baked as early as ancient Egypt.
There are over 200 varieties of bread, differing in ingredients, baking method, and shape.
Low‑calorie breads often contain sugar substitutes and reduced fat content.
Fiber‑rich bread improves digestion and promotes long‑lasting satiety.
White or NFS (No Further Specification) bread is frequently used in diet plans because of its predictable composition.

items.title: Helps lower overall calorie intake
items.content: Reduced fat and sugar content makes this bread a useful tool for cutting daily calories.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Added fibers support gut health, regulate blood sugar, and increase feelings of fullness.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Bread provides a slow release of glucose, stabilising energy levels throughout the day.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast and whole grains supply thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin.

items.title: Low glycemic index (when formulated with whole grains)
items.content: Bran and seed additions lower the glycemic index, beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some reduced‑calorie breads add extra salt to enhance flavor.

items.title: Possible texture changes
items.content: Lower fat and sugar can result in a less soft crumb and milder taste.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use the bread for sandwiches, toast, open‑face snacks, serve alongside soups, or substitute it in recipes to reduce overall calories.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bread in a cool, dry place in an airtight bag or container. For longer storage, freeze it and thaw at room temperature before use.
